title: DESAL-HEART: Hypertonic Saline Added to a Pre-declared Furosemide Dose in Acute Heart Failure
official: DESAL-HEART: Hypertonic Saline Added to a Pre-declared Furosemide Dose in Acute Heart Failure
summary: DESAL-HEART is a multicenter, randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint, mechanistic proof-of-concept trial conducted within the Heart Failure Efficacy and Research Trial (HEART) Platform. The study will evaluate whether adding a single infusion of 3% hypertonic saline solution (HSS) to a pre-declared intravenous furosemide dose improves decongestion in patients hospitalized with acute heart failure.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18 years or older.
* Primary diagnosis of acute heart failure with dyspnea and at least two of the following signs of congestion:

  * Pulmonary congestion on chest radiograph.
  * Rales on chest auscultation.
  * Clinically relevant peripheral edema.
  * Elevated jugular venous pressure.
* Randomization within 24 hours of the hospital admission order or admitted status, with admission to a hospital ward or intensive care unit, including patients remaining in the emergency department awaiting transfer.
* Persistent congestion with a clinical plan for another intravenous furosemide dose.
* NT-proBNP ≥1000 pg/mL, regardless of the presence of atrial fibrillation.
* Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) \>15 mL/min/1.73 m².
* Serum sodium ≥125 mmol/L and \<145 mmol/L.
* Meets the eligibility requirements of the HEART Platform Master Protocol.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Hypertonic saline already administered during the current presentation.
* A clinical indication for therapeutic hypertonic saline.
* Contraindication to either study treatment, including known allergy, hypersensitivity, or intolerance to hypertonic saline or furosemide.
* Requirement for mechanical circulatory support.
* Dialysis-dependent kidney failure or anuria (absence of urine production).
* Treating physician's judgment that either treatment strategy is inappropriate, or any condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, would make participation unsafe or interfere with interpretation of study results.
